paper.title: EXPEREPAIR: Dual-Memory Enhanced LLM-based Repository-Level Program Repair
paper.central_claim: ExpeRepair, an LLM repair framework that accumulates episodic demonstrations and semantic insights from earlier repairs and composes dynamic prompts from them, reaches pass@1 of 60.3% (Lite) and 74.6% (Verified), the best among evaluated open-source methods, with the memory module contributing measurably.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: the Agent tool result exposes no per-call receipt to the worker; model_type is the configured slot (agent_model=haiku -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]) as assigned by the controller.

sections_read: Sec 1-8 (method, setup, results, ablations, sensitivity, discussion, limitation, threats, related work)
missing_sections: Figures 2-7 numeric values not in text package; prompts beyond Sec 2 are on the authors website (not pinned)

evidence.quote: it attempts to reproduce the first five issues from each repository
evidence.support_explanation: Cold-start protocol: memory is seeded from the first five issues of each repository, no external seed data.

evidence.quote: Note that the first five issues, which are used to initialize the semantic and episodic memory components, are also included in the total issues addressed in the standard sequential order of the evaluation to compute the final resolution rate.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory is built from, and the denominator includes, the evaluated benchmark issues themselves in sequential order.

evidence.quote: The successful/failed output refers to whether the test script successfully reproduces the issue (as determined by the LLM) or whether the patch passes the reproduction test.
evidence.support_explanation: Write labels come from self-generated reproduction tests and LLM judgment, not from hidden gold tests.

evidence.quote: REMOVE , to discard contradictory, outdated, or redundant information
evidence.support_explanation: Semantic memory maintenance has explicit ADD/REMOVE/EDIT operations including retirement of redundant or contradictory entries.

evidence.quote: The number of stored insights is capped at 15.
evidence.support_explanation: Hard bound on semantic-memory size.

evidence.quote: removing the Memory Module leads to the most significant performance degradation, with the resolution rate dropping from 48.3% to 42.3% on SWE-Bench Lite and from 57.2% to 50.4% on SWE-Bench Verified
evidence.support_explanation: Store-off control with the same backbone and pipeline: 6.0 pp (about 18 of 300) on Lite and 6.8 pp (34 of 500) on Verified.

evidence.quote: Disabling Episodic Memory also degrades performance notably.
evidence.support_explanation: Component ablation: episodic memory removal costs 3.6 pp (Lite) and 4.4 pp (Verified).

evidence.quote: The resolution rates decrease modestly to 47.0% on Lite and 56.2% on Verified
evidence.support_explanation: Semantic-memory removal costs only 1.3 and 1.0 pp, i.e. 4 and 5 issues; within plausible run-to-run noise.

evidence.quote: We attribute this to the importance of lexical overlap in failure signals
evidence.support_explanation: Mechanism hypothesis explaining why BM25 beats embedding retrieval; testable and tested in Fig 2.

evidence.quote: and report the best-performing results
evidence.support_explanation: Hybrid retrieval alpha is swept and the best value is reported on the benchmark itself.

evidence.quote: Incorporating REMOVE yields substantial gains, particularly on SWE-Bench Verified, improving pass@1 by 3.6 pp over ADD -only.
evidence.support_explanation: Maintenance ablation (ADD only / +EDIT / +REMOVE): pruning matters.

evidence.quote: suggesting a trade-off between retrieval breadth and contextual interference
evidence.support_explanation: Top-k demonstration count and insight count are tuned on the reported benchmarks (k=3, 15 insights).

evidence.quote: For baselines, we directly use the reported results either from the official leaderboard or from the tool’s official paper/repository.
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines are copied from leaderboards with different LLMs, so the SOTA row is not backbone-matched.

evidence.quote: while DARS achieves a pass@1 of 47.0% on SWE-Bench Lite, its average cost is 12.24 USD per instance
evidence.support_explanation: Cost per instance is reported against baselines (ExpeRepair 1.89 USD with Claude 3.5 Sonnet).

evidence.quote: When paired with Claude 4 Sonnet, ExpeRepair further improves performance, achieving 60.3% resolution on SWE-Bench Lite and 74.6% on SWE-Bench Verified.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline numbers use Claude 4 Sonnet with no baseline run on the same backbone.

evidence.quote: the cumulative resolution rates begin to stabilize and gradually improve
evidence.support_explanation: Cumulative-rate curves per repository have no matched no-memory curve; trend is descriptive.

evidence.quote: its effectiveness drops when relevant prior experience is unavailable
evidence.support_explanation: Author-reported boundary: analogy-based retrieval fails on issues needing novel solutions.

evidence.quote: This raises the risk that evaluation results reflect prior exposure rather than genuine generalization.
evidence.support_explanation: Contamination risk acknowledged; mitigation is argued, not measured.

evidence.quote: Current approaches treat each issue in isolation and primarily rely on feedback from the ongoing resolution process
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: no reuse of earlier same-repository repair experience, plus static prompts.

evidence.quote: ExpeL ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) extracts natural language insights and manages them via weighted voting (ADD, EDIT, UPVOTE, DOWNVOTE) for non-parametric learning
evidence.support_explanation: Closest memory neighbor with the same edit-operation maintenance; not run as a baseline.

evidence.quote: a dual-agent architecture with experience banks to improve repair performance
evidence.support_explanation: A baseline already described as having experience banks; its memory is not isolated in comparison.

evidence.quote: In each iteration, we perform multiple samplings with a high temperature to generate diverse candidate patches.
evidence.support_explanation: Test-time sampling and LLM selection add compute; the w/o-memory ablation keeps the pipeline so it controls this.

evidence.quote: Our evaluation is limited to open-source projects implemented in Python
evidence.support_explanation: Scope limitation.

evidence.quote: as manually verified by human annotators
evidence.support_explanation: Reproduction success rate (RSR) is human-verified in ablations, giving a non-LLM check of the memory effect on test generation.

evidence.quote: SWE-Bench Lite consists of 300 GitHub issues sampled from real-world Python projects.
evidence.support_explanation: Denominators: 300 (Lite) and 500 (Verified, our knowledge of the benchmark; text gives only Lite count).

evidence.quote: The combination of Episodic and Semantic Memory yields a synergistic effect
evidence.support_explanation: Claim of synergy rests on single-run differences of a few issues for the semantic part (E008).

signatures.object: episodic memory (per-repository store of repair demonstrations for the test agent and patch agent) and the retrieval-conditioned prompts built from it
signatures.information: issue context plus latest execution feedback as BM25 query; stored (input, successful output) and (input, failed output, feedback, successful output) tuples; hidden SWE-bench tests are not used for labels
signatures.operation: retrieve top-3 demonstrations by BM25 and insert as in-context examples
signatures.output: dynamic experience-driven prompt for test generation and patch generation
signatures.conditions: per-repository memory, up to 3 trials x 4 patches, cold start from first five issues
signatures.feedback: self-generated reproduction test pass/fail and execution results
signatures.selection_rule: a demonstration is written as success if the generated reproduction test reproduces the issue (LLM-judged) or the patch passes the reproduction test
signatures.persistence: appended after each issue; stored with issue description, status and timestamp
signatures.later_use: later issues in the same repository in dataset chronological order
signatures.claimed_effect: pass@1 48.3 (Lite) / 57.2 (Verified) with Claude 3.5 Sonnet; 60.3 / 74.6 with Claude 4 Sonnet
signatures.failure_boundary: drops when no analogous prior issue exists; k>3 interferes; dense retrieval worse than BM25

signatures.object: semantic memory: at most 15 natural-language insights per agent role appended to the system prompt
signatures.information: complete repair trajectory (issue, tests, patches, test results before/after); existing insights
signatures.operation: LLM summarizes why attempts succeeded/failed then applies ADD / REMOVE / EDIT (max four ops per role per issue; REMOVE required before ADD at the cap)
signatures.selection_rule: LLM judgment of novelty, contradiction, duplication; no utility measurement
signatures.later_use: all insights prepended to the task prompt of every later issue
signatures.claimed_effect: smaller gain than episodic: +1.3 / +1.0 pp (Table 2); REMOVE +3.6 pp over ADD-only on Verified
signatures.failure_boundary: accumulation without REMOVE saturates prompt and adds noise

gap.author_gap: Repository-level LLM repair treats each issue in isolation and relies on static handcrafted prompts, ignoring recurring bug patterns and project conventions from earlier resolved issues.
gap.checked_gap: Specific and plausible for SWE-bench-style streams of same-repository issues; evidenced by the memory-off drop (E006) rather than by an independent analysis of baseline failures. OpenHands is already described as having experience banks (E021), so isolation-of-issues is not universally true of baselines.

matches.reason: Successful and corrected-failed repair records are stored as cases, retrieved by lexical similarity, adapted in context, and appended after each issue (H03).

claims.text: A dual episodic+semantic memory with dynamic prompt composition raises repository-level repair pass@1.
claims.setting: SWE-Bench Lite (300) and Verified; Claude 3.5 Sonnet (+o4-mini fallback)
claims.baseline_control: same pipeline without memory / without episodic / without semantic
claims.selection_vs_test: memory built online from the evaluated issues in dataset order (first five per repo as seed); hyper-parameters tuned on reported scores
claims.allowed_conclusion: In an online stream over SWE-bench issues, enabling the memory module raises pass@1 by about 6-7 points with the pipeline otherwise fixed.

claims.text: ExpeRepair achieves best performance among evaluated open-source methods (60.3 / 74.6).
claims.allowed_conclusion: With Claude 3.5 Sonnet it exceeds listed open-source methods that also use Claude 3.5 Sonnet or weaker; the Claude 4 row is not matched.
Variants without REMOVE score lower (+3.6 pp for full vs ADD-only on Verified).

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Within an online SWE-bench stream, persisted episodic demonstrations (and, weakly, curated insights) raise later-issue resolution by about 6 points over a memory-off run of the same pipeline; dual-memory synergy and the SOTA headline are only partially supported.
unresolved: Single-run effects of 1-5 pp for semantic memory
Memory-on compute vs memory-off not tabulated

G.reason: Concrete, domain-specific gap (same-repository recurring patterns plus static prompts), stated neighbors in memory and APR literatures, but differentiation from ExpeL/OpenHands experience banks is argued not tested and residual (localization) is only a limitation note.

M.reason: Operation-to-problem fit is explicit: query includes execution feedback so failure-signal-matched demonstrations are retrieved, BM25 chosen for lexical error overlap and tested; insights split by role; predicts failure when no analogue exists (reported).

X.reason: Write rule, labels, update ops, cap, retrieval method, trial counts, cold-start and prompts are all specified and ablated; missing: versioning/rollback, utility-based admission, role of seed issues in leakage.

E.measurement.reason: SWE-bench pass@1 against hidden tests is a credible verifier, labels used for memory are not the gold tests, and RSR is human-verified; downgraded by leaderboard baselines on unmatched backbones and unaddressed benchmark contamination.

E.causality.reason: Same-pipeline memory-off, episodic-off and semantic-off ablations on two benchmarks plus retrieval and update-operation ablations; lacks a compute-matched or random-demonstration control, a no-memory longitudinal curve and a cross-repository memory control.

E.holdout.reason: Labels are not gold and issues arrive in dataset order, but memory is built from the scored issues, hyper-parameters (k, cap, alpha) are tuned on reported scores and contamination is argued not measured.

E.statistics.reason: Denominators (300/500) and unique-solve counts are given and negative boundary cases are reported, but single runs with no intervals; semantic-memory effect is 4-5 issues.

E.cost.reason: Per-instance cost reported against baselines (1.89 USD) but memory-off cost, seed-phase and memory-update LLM calls not separated, and candidate-sampling/LLM-selection compute is not matched with baselines.

rationale: Clear online dual-memory loop with write rules, maintenance ops and same-pipeline ablations showing about +6 points; held back by benchmark-stream memory construction, test-tuned hyper-parameters, unmatched SOTA baselines and single runs.
